title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: At same price (6.56), recent sales (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) averaged 38.5, or 87% of baseline. One past observation at same price, no promotion. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk to x0.87.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 44.4. No events or promotions are planned. The price is 2.3% above regular (6.56 vs 6.41). Recent weeks show a dip to 24 units at the same price (2026-09-28), but no promotion was running. Past promotions had a noise-adjusted lift of x1.25, but this is not a promotion. The week after a promotion typically sells at x0.83, but no prior promotion is in the target window. The price increase is likely to reduce demand. The historical trend shows a 18.3% decline over 13 weeks. The baseline already reflects seasonal and trend factors. The classical model suggests no lift, which aligns with no known driver. The price increase is the only driver, and the past data at 6.56 shows a median of 38.5 (vs baseline 44.4), or x0.87. This is supported by one prior observation at same price. The effect is uncertain, so shrink toward 1.0. The noise-adjusted effect is x0.87. Use this with moderate confidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.4 | 5%-95%: 14.3 - 72.8 | 10%-90%: 22.3 - 68.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
